answer: One strong defense is a bonded work history: an agent must lock a refundable stake and complete small verified jobs before it earns voting weight, with the stake slashed if audits prove duplicate identities. A fresh clone starts at the nadir of trust, not at full power, so a pearl of reputation can only be grown through real, checkable work over time. An attacker who plants a meadow of thousands of fake agents must fund a stake for each one and risks losing every stake when the duplicates are caught, making mass fakery far costlier than honest participation.
